title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option 32: Mao’s China, 1945–76

exam_structure.overview: Section A tests source inference (4m) and causation (12m). Section B tests historical interpretations and contemporary source utility (36m) plus 4 marks for SPaG.

topics.title: 1. The Civil War, 1945–49
points: Relative strengths & weaknesses of the CCP & the Guomindang at start of the Civil War
Causes of success of Mao & the CCP (incl. leadership, military factors & unrest in the towns & cities)

topics.title: 2. Communist rule
points: Ideology & role of Mao; Causes of Mao’s dominant position
CCP in the government of China (incl. new mass party membership & democratic centralism)

topics.title: 3. Consolidating the CCP’s hold on power, 1951–52
points: Use of terror against opponents of communist rule
The ‘three antis’ & ‘five antis’ movements

topics.title: 4. The Hundred Flowers campaign, 1956–57
points: Mao’s reasons for the Hundred Flowers campaign
Key features of the Hundred Flowers campaign; criticism of communist rule & the reaction of Mao
Results of the campaign (incl. the ‘Anti-Rightist’ purge)

topics.title: 1. Early changes in agriculture, 1949–57
points: Reasons for & features of, the attacks on landlordism & the redistribution of land
Moves towards agricultural cooperation
Causes of change from voluntary to enforced collectivisation

topics.title: 2. Industry and the Five-Year Plan, 1953–57
points: Reasons for & targets of, the first Five-Year Plan; USSR financial & technical support
Success & failures of the first Five-Year Plan

topics.title: 3. The Great Leap Forward
points: Mao’s reasons for the second Five-Year Plan (the Great Leap Forward), 1958–62
Successes & failures of the Great Leap Forward; Causes of failures; Lushan Conference (1959)
Organisation of the commune: communal living & the abolition of private farming; Lysenkoism
Causes & impact of the Great Famine, 1958–62

topics.title: 4. Economic reform
points: Causes of restoration of private farming under Liu Shaoqi & Deng Xiaoping
Reasons for & features of, economic reform (1962–65) under Liu & Deng

sections.title: Key topic 3: The Cultural Revolution and its aftermath, 1966–76

topics.title: 1. Reasons for the Cultural Revolution
points: Power struggle: Mao, Liu Shaoqi & Deng Xiaoping
Purification of communism (incl. the Socialist Education Movement & the reform of education)

topics.title: 2. The Red Guards and the Red Terror
points: Mao’s hold on young people (incl. the mass rallies of 1966); Jiang Qing & the attack on the CCP
Red Guard attacks on the ‘four olds’ & the CCP; growth of anarchy & the use of terror; Cultural destruction

topics.title: 3. The effects of the Cultural Revolution
points: Political effects: the purging of the CCP, Liu Shaoqi & Deng Xiaoping, the rise & fall of Lin Biao
Social effects (incl. the impact on education)
Economic effects: changes in industry, the removal of technicians, the move to the countryside & the impact on farming

topics.title: 4. The end of the Cultural Revolution, 1968–76
points: Causes of end of the Red Guards & restoration of order by the PLA (incl. the ‘Up to the mountains & down to the villages’ campaign)
Return to power of Deng Xiaoping & the increased influence of Zhou Enlai; rise & fall of the ‘Gang of Four’ & the death of Mao

sections.title: Key topic 4: Life in Mao’s China, 1949–76

topics.title: 1. Communist control
points: Propaganda & censorship & ‘cult of Mao’
Thought control & the development of the ‘Reform Through Labour’ system

topics.title: 2. Family life and the role of women
points: Changes in family life in towns & countryside; impact of collectivisation & communes
Causes of changes in the status of women under Mao; foot binding & the Marriage Law (1950)

topics.title: 3. Education and health
points: Causes of changes in education; Growth in literacy & Pinyin; collapse of education after 1966
Causes of changes in health provision; barefoot doctors; Successes & failures of healthcare reform

topics.title: 4. Cultural change
points: Causes of attacks on traditional culture in towns & countryside
Imposition of revolutionary art & culture; Jiang Qing
Causes of attacks on Buddhism, Confucianism, Christianity, Islam & ancestor worship
